proofs.full_local_argument:
LOCAL REPAIR, not a quotation or a claim of author correction. Fix mu1,mu2,D>0 and an integer budget m>=1. Set N=2m, d=3m and Delta=3mu1/(2mu2). Translate coordinates by the algorithm's initial query, so y_1=0. Define g(z)=|z|^3/3 for |z|<=Delta and g(z)=Delta*z^2-Delta^2*|z|+Delta^3/3 otherwise. The values and first two derivatives match at +/-Delta. Thus g is C2, g(0)=g'(0)=g''(0)=0, g''(z)=2min(Delta,|z|), g'' is 2-Lipschitz, and g' is strictly increasing and unbounded. For z>0, g''(z)>0 and g'(z)>0.
For any n orthonormal vectors v_1,...,v_n, define F_n(y)=(mu2/12)[g(<v_1,y>)+g(<v_n,y>)+sum_{i=1}^{n-1}g(<v_i-v_(i+1),y>)-gamma<v_1,y>], with the same gamma>0 throughout the comparisons. For n=1 the endpoint term is counted twice. In orthonormal coordinates x, put H_n(x)=g(x_1)+g(x_n)+sum g(x_i-x_(i+1))-gamma*x_1. Orthogonal projection gives min F_n=(mu2/12)min H_n, with a minimizer of the same norm as x. These are actual orthogonal embeddings, unlike the printed repeated-tail assignment.
Endpoint smoothness, including both endpoints: let the multiset of vectors a be v_1,v_n and v_i-v_(i+1) for 1<=i<n. For every u, sum_a <a,u>^2 <=4||u||^2. For n>=2 this follows by (x_i-x_(i+1))^2<=2x_i^2+2x_(i+1)^2: endpoint coefficients are at most 3 and interior coefficients at most 4; orthogonal complement coordinates contribute zero. For n=1 the sum is 2x_1^2. Also ||a||<=sqrt(2). The Hessian is (mu2/12)sum_a g''(<a,y>)aa^T, hence is positive semidefinite and has norm at most (mu2/12)*2Delta*4=mu1. For h=y-z and any unit u, the absolute quadratic form of the Hessian difference is at most (mu2/12)sum_a 2|<a,h>|<a,u>^2 <=(2sqrt(2)/3)mu2||h|| <=mu2||h||. The operator norm of a symmetric matrix equals its maximum absolute unit quadratic form. Thus F_n is convex C2 with globally mu1-Lipschitz gradient and mu2-Lipschitz Hessian. The linear term changes neither bound. Translation changes none of these properties.
Exact minimizers without Proposition 3: for each real s>=1 let delta_s>0 be the unique solution g'(s*delta_s)+g'(delta_s)=gamma. Existence and uniqueness follow from continuity and strict increase from 0 to infinity as delta increases. For integer n, the vector x_i=(n+1-i)delta_n has zero gradient in H_n: all consecutive differences and x_n equal delta_n, interior derivatives cancel, and the first equation is g'(n*delta_n)+g'(delta_n)=gamma. For n=1 the equation is 2g'(delta_1)=gamma. Convexity proves global minimality. Strict convexity of g and injectivity of the endpoint/difference map prove uniqueness. Consequently E(n):=min H_n=g(n*delta_n)+n*g(delta_n)-gamma*n*delta_n, and the minimizer norm squared is delta_n^2*S_n, where S_n=sum_{k=1}^n k^2.
Uniform minimum comparison: extend E(s)=g(s*delta_s)+s*g(delta_s)-gamma*s*delta_s to real s>=1. The implicit equation has positive derivative s*g''(s*delta_s)+g''(delta_s) in delta, so delta_s and E(s) are C1, including regime boundaries. At fixed positive delta the left side increases with s, so delta_s is decreasing. Differentiation, cancelling the delta_s derivative by its defining equation, gives E'(s)=g(delta_s)-delta_s*g'(delta_s)=-h(delta_s), where h(z)=z*g'(z)-g(z). For z>0, h'(z)=z*g''(z)>0. Directly h(z)=2z^3/3 for z<=Delta and h(z)=Delta*z^2-Delta^3/3 for z>=Delta; therefore h(z)>=(2/3)min{z^3,Delta*z^2}. It follows that E(m)-E(N)=integral_m^N h(delta_s)ds >=m*h(delta_N). Also E(t)>=E(m) for integers 1<=t<=m. This calculation covers every positive gamma and Delta and every m>=1; it uses none of the printed three-regime inequalities.
Distance and free-parameter calibration: set delta=D/sqrt(S_N) and gamma=g'(N*delta)+g'(delta)>0. Then delta_N=delta and the minimizer of F_N has norm exactly D. Since S_N<=N^3 for N>=1 (each of N terms k^2 is at most N^2), delta>=D/(2m)^(3/2). Combining with the preceding step and multiplying only once by mu2/12 yields min F_m-min F_N >=(mu2/18)m*min{delta^3,Delta*delta^2} >=min{mu2*D^3/(18*2^(9/2)*m^(7/2)),mu1*D^2/(96*m^2)} >=(1/1000)min{mu2*D^3/m^(7/2),mu1*D^2/m^2}. Here mu2*Delta=3mu1/2 and 18*2^(9/2)<1000. This uniform bound includes small budgets and all relationships among D,Delta,m. It does not rely on the erroneous mu2 factor in the unscaled table. In the all-cubic regime the same minimizer formula independently gives E(n)=-(2/3)gamma^(3/2)n/sqrt(1+n^2), before the separate mu2/12 scaling.
Oracle realization and complete orthogonal completion: choose v_t after query y_t is determined, for t=1,...,m, perpendicular to y_1,...,y_t and all previously chosen v's. There are at most 2t-1 linear constraints, fewer than d=3m, so a unit choice exists. Reply with the value, gradient and Hessian of the eventual F_N. These replies are already well-defined without choosing the tail: require every later v_j to be perpendicular to y_1,...,y_t. Then at y_t every tail difference indexed i>=t and the last endpoint have zero argument, with g,g',g'' all zero. The first endpoint involves only v_1; the difference i=t-1 may involve v_t, which is already fixed. Thus the replies do not depend on any future vector. Determinism fixes the next query, closing the induction for arbitrary queries, including those outside revealed spans. After query m, choose v_(m+1),...,v_N as an orthonormal family in the complement of span{y_1,...,y_m,v_1,...,v_m}; its dimension is at least 3m-2m=m. These choices preserve every reply and make all N vectors orthonormal. This is a single fixed admissible function consistent with the entire simulated transcript. Extend the deterministic run afterward with its ordinary exact Oracle.
For each t<=m the completed vectors satisfy <v_j,y_t>=0 for all j>=t. Therefore F_N(y_t)=F_t(y_t), since the replaced endpoint at v_t and all removed tail terms vanish in value. For t=1 both sides are zero at y_1=0. Hence F_N(y_t)-min F_N >=min F_t-min F_N =(mu2/12)(E(t)-E(N)) >=min F_m-min F_N. This proves the quantitative error bound simultaneously for every one of the first m queries, without a support restriction on the algorithm. The witness minimizer is sum_i (N+1-i)delta*v_i, of norm D; translating back gives distance D from the original initial query.
Final quantifiers and accuracy: put Q=min{sqrt(mu1*D^2/epsilon),(mu2*D^3/epsilon)^(2/7)}. If Q>=64 choose m=floor(Q/64)>=1. Since m<=Q/64, both entries in the minimum error bound are at least 64^2*epsilon: the gradient-scale entry uses Q<=sqrt(mu1*D^2/epsilon), and the Hessian-scale entry uses Q<=(mu2*D^3/epsilon)^(2/7) and 64^(7/2)>=64^2. Thus all first m queries have error at least (4096/1000)epsilon>epsilon. The first accurate index is at least m+1>Q/64. If Q<64, the source's index convention gives every queried output index at least 1>Q/64; any admissible constant function witnesses this trivial bound. This supplies universal c=1/64 for every positive parameter tuple. Only finite d=3m is needed in the nontrivial case. No randomized extension, fixed-d result, computational-cost bound, or guarantee for an arbitrary unqueried output is asserted.

assumptions: f is convex and twice differentiable on all of R^d.
For every x,y in R^d, ||gradient f(x)-gradient f(y)|| <= mu1||x-y|| and ||Hessian f(x)-Hessian f(y)||_op <= mu2||x-y||.
There is a global minimizer w* with ||w_1-w*|| <= D.
Access is through the stated Oracle; no linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.
statement.conclusion: There is a universal c>0 such that the worst-case query index required to obtain f(w_T)-min f <= epsilon is at least c min{sqrt(mu1 D^2/epsilon),(mu2 D^3/epsilon)^(2/7)}. The local argument supplies c=1/64 under the source convention that the initial query has index 1.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Unconstrained minimization of f:R^d -> R. Vector norms are Euclidean; Hessian norm is the induced operator norm. The exact second-order Oracle at w returns f(w), gradient f(w), and Hessian f(w). Queries w_1,w_2,... are deterministic functions of preceding Oracle replies.
statement.parameter_domains: mu1>0, mu2>0, D>0, epsilon>0. Some finite dimension d, not necessarily fixed independently of the parameters. Theorem 2 states no further parameter window.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every positive mu1,mu2,D,epsilon and every deterministic Oracle algorithm of Section 2.1, there exists a finite dimension and an admissible function, with a minimizer within D of its initial query, on which its first epsilon-accurate queried point has the stated index lower bound. Dimension may depend on parameters and the budget. No randomized extension is claimed.
